testName: Air Brakes Test #2 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What can happen if you do not drain the tanks in an air brake system?

options.text: Water can freeze and cause the brakes to fail.
The brakes become soft and squishy.
Too much air collects in the system.
Too much fuel is carried in the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Water can freeze and cause the brakes to fail.
questions.explanation: Air brake system tanks must be drained to remove water and compressor oil. If you don't drain them, water can build up in the system. In cold weather, this water can freeze and cause the brakes to fail.

questions.question: How can you check if a trailer has ABS?

options.text: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
Look under the hood for an ABS sticker.
Remove a tire and look for the ABS sensor on the axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look under the trailer for wheel speed sensors attached to the back of the brakes.
questions.explanation: To check if a trailer has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), look under the vehicle. You will find the electronic control unit and wheel speed sensor wires attached to the back of the brakes.

questions.question: What should you do if the low pressure warning light comes on while driving?

options.text: You can only brake if there is enough air left in the tanks.
You can brake 14 times before the air runs out.
Continue driving normally and check the brakes later.
Continue driving but turn on the emergency flashers to warn others.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can only brake if there is enough air left in the tanks.
questions.explanation: If the low air pressure warning light comes on, stop and safely park your vehicle as soon as possible. Braking will only work as long as there is enough air remaining in the tanks.

questions.question: Which braking system does the brake pedal control?
questions.explanation: The service brake system is controlled by the brake pedal. When you press it, the brakes are applied during normal driving.

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, what happens if one system has a leak?

options.text: Both systems will always have leaks.
The leak may not affect the other system.
There is no need to worry about it.
The leak will affect the other system.

questions.correctAnswerText: The leak may not affect the other system.
questions.explanation: A dual air brake system has two separate air brake systems. If one system has a leak, it may not affect the other system.

questions.question: How do you set the parking brake on newer vehicles?

options.text: Move a lever to the right.
Push in the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
Pull out the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
Pull up on the steering column.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull out the yellow, diamond-shaped knob.
questions.explanation: On newer vehicles with air brakes, the parking brake uses a yellow, diamond-shaped knob. Pull the knob out to set the brakes. Push it in to release them.

questions.question: How much air pressure should build up before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes?
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, wait for the air compressor to build at least 100 psi of pressure in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: At 55 mph on dry pavement, how much extra distance does brake lag add to your stopping distance?
questions.explanation: Total stopping distance has four parts: perception distance, reaction distance, brake lag distance, and braking distance. When braking at 55 mph on dry pavement, brake lag adds about 32 feet to your total stopping distance.

questions.question: When you press the brake pedal in a vehicle with S-cam brakes, air pressure pushes out the rod and moves what?
questions.explanation: When you press the brake pedal in a vehicle with S-cam brakes, air enters the brake chambers. This air pressure pushes out the rods and moves the slack adjusters, which twist the brake camshafts.

questions.question: How should you set the front brake limiting valve for normal stopping power?

options.text: Set the control to the off position.
Keep the control at the halfway mark.

questions.explanation: Some vehicles made before 1975 have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. The valve was meant to reduce front-wheel skidding on slippery surfaces. However, research shows this is not needed. Keep the valve set to "normal".

questions.question: In a dual air brake system, what is true?

options.text: Both systems share the same air tanks.
Each system has its own separate air tanks.
You must choose which system to use.
Brakes work on only one side of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each system has its own separate air tanks.
questions.explanation: Heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brake systems connected by one set of brake controls. Each system has its own air tanks.

questions.question: If the air pressure warning light comes on, what should you do?

options.text: Drive with one foot on the gas and one foot on the brake.
Safely pull over and stop the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely pull over and stop the vehicle.
questions.explanation: When the low air pressure warning activates, stop your vehicle safely while you can still control the brakes.

questions.question: When should the low air pressure warning activate?

options.text: When tank pressure drops below 120 psi.
When tank pressure drops below 60 psi.
When tank pressure drops below 10 psi.

questions.correctAnswerText: When tank pressure drops below 60 psi.
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning must activate when air pressure falls below 60 psi. The warning can be a light, buzzer, or wig wag.

questions.question: How should you brake in an emergency?

options.text: Lock the wheels and skid to a stop.
Keep the vehicle going straight while braking.
Expect the vehicle to slow down faster than normal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the vehicle going straight while braking.
questions.explanation: Use controlled braking or stab braking for emergency stops. Brake in a way that keeps your vehicle straight while letting you steer if needed.

questions.question: The ____ shows how much pressure is in the air tanks.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with air brakes must have a supply pressure gauge. This gauge tells the driver how much air pressure is in each air tank.

questions.question: What is the controlled braking method?

options.text: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
Press the brakes with about half force.
Press the brakes until the wheels lock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the brakes as hard as possible without locking the wheels.
questions.explanation: Controlled braking means pressing the brakes as hard as you can without locking the wheels. If you need to steer while braking, release the brakes, steer, then brake again.

questions.question: When only the tractor has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what happens?

options.text: The brakes work less effectively without ABS.

questions.explanation: When only the tractor has ABS and the trailer does not, jackknifing risk is reduced and steering control is maintained. If only the trailer has ABS, it is less likely to swing out.

questions.question: What is a wig wag?

options.text: A tube that moves air from the compressor to the tanks
A noise made when air brakes are used
A part that lets air flow freely in the brake unit

questions.explanation: A wig wag is a low air pressure warning device. It drops a mechanical arm into the driver's view when air pressure falls below 60 psi.

questions.question: If brake pads rub against the drums and create too much heat, what happens?

options.text: The air compressor cools the brakes.

questions.explanation: Excessive heat from brake use causes expansion and chemical changes that make brakes less effective. Eventually they may stop working. This is called "brake fade."

questions.question: Emergency brakes are required on what vehicles?

options.text: They are not required on trucks.
They are only required on trailers.

questions.explanation: All trucks, truck tractors, and buses must have emergency brakes and parking brakes. These brakes must be held by mechanical force.

questions.question: How often should you drain air tanks that have manual drains?
questions.explanation: Drain air tanks with manual drains at the end of each day. This removes oil and water that build up in the tanks.

questions.question: During a static leakage test, what is the maximum air leakage allowed for a triple combination vehicle with air brakes in one minute?
questions.explanation: The maximum leakage rate is 5 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, do not drive the vehicle. It needs repairs.

questions.question: What is the purpose of air tank drains?

options.text: Allow rain water to enter an air tank.
Remove water and oil from an air tank.

questions.correctAnswerText: Remove water and oil from an air tank.
questions.explanation: Compressed air contains water and compressor oil. These build up in the tank and can damage the brakes. Open manual drains daily to remove this buildup.

questions.question: When should you use the parking brake?

options.text: Every time you park the vehicle.
To stop the vehicle during normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Every time you park the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park your vehicle.

questions.question: What type of air brake system do most heavy-duty vehicles use?
questions.explanation: Most heavy-duty vehicles use dual air brake systems. This system has two separate air brake systems that share one set of controls.
